headline: Harding died in office, an earthquake levelled Tokyo, and a German mark stopped meaning anything
texture: Warren Harding died in San Francisco and Calvin Coolidge became president on August 2. The Great Kanto earthquake destroyed Tokyo and Yokohama on September 1 and killed more than a hundred thousand people, and in the weeks after it mobs murdered ethnic Koreans across the region. Hyperinflation in Germany reached its peak on November 15, by which point a mark bought nothing at all.

Hitler tried to seize power in Munich on November 8 and was arrested three days later. TIME magazine put out its first issue on March 3. Roy and Walt Disney set up a studio in October under their own name. Coolidge addressed Congress in December in the first radio broadcast from the Capitol, which is a sentence that would have meant nothing three years earlier.

Cecil B. DeMille's The Ten Commandments took $4,169,798 in rentals, the year's biggest, with The Covered Wagon behind it. Harold Lloyd hung off a clock face in Safety Last! and tied for third with The Hunchback of Notre Dame. Yankee Stadium opened on April 18, and in October the Yankees beat the Giants in the World Series after losing to them twice.
